description: Packed snow with two dark eyes, heavier than snow should be. Every spike it throws is grown out of itself.
lore: Low in this country the ground does not stay put. A path takes itself somewhere else between one season and the next; a hill everybody was certain of turns out not to be there, and there is no saying when it stopped. High under the crystal country none of that happens. The snow up there has not needed correcting in a very long time, and there is also hardly anyone left up there to walk on it. What comes up out of that combination is packed harder than anything down in the grass.

It is snow pressed into a shape with two dark eyes set well into it, and it weighs more than snow has any business weighing. What it is packed from does not melt: a handful of the blue-white pebbles that come off one will sit in a warm palm all afternoon and be exactly as cold when it is put down. The parts keep. The whole one does not.

It arms itself out of itself. A spike comes up through the top, grows to a point, and goes — and there is measurably less creature afterwards than there was before it started. It will do that until there is not enough left to do it with, because there is nothing up there to show it another way and nothing in it that could be shown. At the end it does not shatter, which is what people expect and would be easier to watch. It slumps. The shape gives up its edges and goes down into a lump of slush inside its own footprint, and the wet mark outlasts the rest of it by an hour.

In the slush lies a pale blue stone rimed white, cold to hold and staying cold, and warm underneath that in the way they all are. In a blade it puts winter into the hit, and every so often — not reliably, and never on the swing you were counting on — whatever took the hit goes heavy-footed for a while, as though it had walked further uphill than it meant to and only just noticed. That is the high ground pressed down to the size of a fist: the part of the world that has not gone anywhere, standing about in the drifts in quantity, on a road that has stopped having anyone on it.
